title: Monitoring & Notifications
subtitle: Job summaries, Slack alerts on failure, status badges, and if: failure() — close the feedback loop on every deployment

content.text: CI visibility — knowing what happened and why

A CI pipeline that runs silently is only half useful. When a deployment succeeds, you want your team notified so they can verify behavior in production. When it fails at 2am, the on-call engineer needs a Slack message, not an email buried in their inbox. When stakeholders ask 'is CI passing?', a badge in the README answers instantly. Visibility is the last mile of a great CI/CD setup.
Job summaries — rich reports in the GitHub UI

content.code:
- name: Generate test summary
  if: always()   # run even if tests failed
  run: |
    # $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is a Markdown file rendered in the workflow run UI
    echo '## Test Results' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo '' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

    # Parse test output and format as a table
    PASSED=$(grep -c 'PASS' test-results.txt || echo 0)
    FAILED=$(grep -c 'FAIL' test-results.txt || echo 0)
    TOTAL=$((PASSED + FAILED))

    echo "| Status | Count |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "| --- | --- |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "| ✅ Passed | $PASSED |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "| ❌ Failed | $FAILED |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "| 📊 Total | $TOTAL |" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

    if [ $FAILED -gt 0 ]; then
      echo '' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
      echo '### Failed Tests' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
      grep 'FAIL' test-results.txt >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    fi

- name: Add deployment summary
  run: |
    echo "## 🚀 Deployment" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- **Environment:** ${{ inputs.environment }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- **URL:** ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- **Image:** \`ghcr.io/myorg/myapp:${{ github.sha }}\`" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
    echo "- **Deployed by:** ${{ github.actor }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Deploy
        id: deploy
        run: ./deploy.sh

      # Always runs — success or failure
      - name: Notify Slack
        if: always()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "text": "${{ job.status == 'success' && '✅' || '🚨' }} Deploy to ${{ inputs.environment }}",
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": "*${{ job.status == 'success' && '✅ Deploy succeeded' || '🚨 Deploy FAILED' }}*\nEnvironment: ${{ inputs.environment }}\nBranch: ${{ github.ref_name }}\nBy: ${{ github.actor }}\n<${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}|View workflow run>"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE: INCOMING_WEBHOOK

      # Only notify on failure — for always-failing alerts on a critical service
      - name: Page on-call on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          curl -X POST ${{ secrets.PAGERDUTY_WEBHOOK }} \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            -d '{"message": "Production deploy failed: ${{ github.run_id }}"}'

content.text: Conditional steps — if: failure(), if: success(), if: always()

content.code:
steps:
  - name: Deploy
    run: ./deploy.sh

  # Runs only if ALL previous steps succeeded
  - name: Run smoke tests
    if: success()   # this is also the default — 'if: success()' is implicit
    run: ./smoke-test.sh

  # Runs only if a previous step failed
  - name: Rollback on failure
    if: failure()
    run: ./rollback.sh --version ${{ env.PREVIOUS_VERSION }}

  # Runs regardless of whether previous steps succeeded or failed
  - name: Upload logs
    if: always()
    uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
    with:
      name: deploy-logs
      path: logs/

  # Runs if a SPECIFIC step failed (using its id)
  - name: Alert if deploy specifically failed
    if: steps.deploy.outcome == 'failure'
    run: echo "Deploy step failed specifically"

  # Combine conditions:
  - name: Only alert on main branch failures
    if: failure() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    run: ./alert.sh

content.text: Don't alert on every PR failure — only on main. Developers expect some PRs to fail CI while they're working on a fix. Notifying Slack on every PR failure creates noise that trains people to ignore alerts. Reserve Slack/PagerDuty notifications for: (1) failures on the main branch, (2) production deployment failures, (3) scheduled security scans. Use if: failure() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' to scope alerts correctly.

questions.question: A workflow has steps: Build → Test → Deploy. 'Test' fails. Which steps run with 'if: always()'?
options: Only steps explicitly marked 'if: always()' run — Build, Test, and any step with if: always()
All steps run regardless — 'if: always()' on the workflow level overrides all step conditions
Build ran before the failure, Test failed, Deploy is skipped. Steps with 'if: always()' run even though Test failed.
No steps run after a failure unless the entire job has 'continue-on-error: true'
questions.explanation: When Test fails: Build already ran (it ran before the failure). Test failed — that step is done. Deploy has no 'if' condition, so it defaults to 'if: success()' — it is SKIPPED because Test failed. Steps with 'if: always()' run regardless of the failure. This is why you mark cleanup, artifact upload, and notification steps with 'if: always()' — you want them to run whether the job succeeds or fails.

faq.q: How do I avoid duplicate Slack notifications when multiple jobs in a workflow fail?
faq.a: Add a dedicated 'notify' job at the end of the workflow that depends on all other jobs with 'needs: [build, test, deploy]'. Give it 'if: failure()' at the job level. This job runs only if any upstream job failed, and sends a single notification summarizing the entire workflow run. It avoids one notification per job.

examples: Shopify's engineering team has a dedicated Slack channel for production deployment notifications — every deploy posts a summary with the deployer's name, the version, and a link. This creates accountability and gives the team a shared real-time view of what's being shipped

Job summaries made GitHub Actions dramatically more useful for test-heavy projects: instead of scrolling through hundreds of log lines to find which test failed, the summary shows a formatted table of results directly on the workflow run page
